short: Chin-aimed radar and an envelope + GMM-HMM front end are standard; the binary rest-vs-touch task shows some closed-mouth movement, not tongue-specific sensing.
position: The paper changes radar placement (M05, chin instead of mouth) and the front end (M06, RMS envelope into GMM-HMMs); both are standard. The chin placement is rare but untested against a mouth-facing radar, and the authors' later two-radar study found the chin-facing radar worse, with it placed farther away. The envelope beats CLEAN for all four participants, but feature and classifier change together. A binary rest-versus-palate-touch task with co-moving throat muscles shows detection of closed-mouth movement, not tongue-specific sensing; evaluation (M12) is within-participant leave-one-out on 40 trials for 4 participants, one an author.
